title: Window previews appear at different speeds
line: Moving the pointer from one task manager icon to the next now always hands the tooltip straight over instead of sometimes closing it and waiting the full delay again.
explanation: When a tooltip is open, the task manager's TriangleMouseFilter holds back the next icon's hover enter for up to 300 ms if the pointer moves sideways near the top of the icons (it may be heading for the tooltip). It let the old icon's hover leave through, though, so the old tooltip was dismissed and closed after 200 ms; when the held enter finally arrived no tooltip was visible and the new icon started the full show delay, about 1 s with nothing shown. Whether a move gets held depends on its path, hence the inconsistency. The filter now also holds the old item's hover leave while an enter is held and sends it right before that enter (or as soon as the hold ends any other way), so the old tooltip stays open and the new icon takes it over at once.

commits.message:
trianglemousefilter: hold the previous item's hover leave with the enter

The filter held back the next item's hover enter but let the old item's
hover leave through, so the old task tooltip closed before the new one
could reuse it. Hold that leave too and send it just before the enter.

BUG: 513390

media.caption: Master: hovering Info Center, then three quick sideways moves near the top of the icons (System Monitor, Spectacle, Plasma Engine Explorer). Each time the old tooltip fades out and the new one appears about 1 s later.
With the fix, same moves: the old tooltip stays until the new one replaces it, never empty.
Frames every 100 ms, pointer reaches System Monitor at +0.0 s: Info Center fades out, nothing from +0.6 to +1.0 s, System Monitor at +1.1 s.
Same frames with the fix: Info Center stays while the filter holds the move, System Monitor replaces it at +0.3 s.

reviews.text: Clean root-cause fix in TriangleMouseFilter: holding the previous item's HoverLeave while a new item's HoverEnter is intercepted and flushing it immediately before resending or passing through the enter keeps the tooltip open for instant handover instead of letting ToolTipDialog::dismiss() close it during the 300 ms hold. Lifetime safety is handled via QPointer<QQuickItem> and std::exchange, all exit paths flush held leaves, and the before/after frame strips and regression checks (diagonal glides, Kickoff, tst_triangleFilter) convincingly prove the fix.
